summary:
**Flamewise** is an interactive intelligence dashboard that makes NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to discover, explore, and understand. I developed a data driven platform that connects directly to NASA's Physical Sciences and Aerospace Research (PSA) experiments, collecting and organizing over 12 GB of research data.

The dashboard transforms complex scientific information into interactive visualizations, allowing users to search research, explore experimental findings, and identify patterns through charts rather than relying solely on lengthy technical documents. It also makes different types of data easier to interpret through appropriate visual representations.

By bridging the gap between large scientific datasets and accessible visual exploration, Flamewise helps researchers and curious learners navigate decades of combustion research more efficiently. It is important because making existing scientific knowledge discoverable and understandable can accelerate research, support better insights, and make valuable NASA research accessible to a wider audience.
details:
Flamewise: NASA Combustion Research Explorer

Flamewise is an interactive research dashboard that makes NASA’s microgravity combustion research easier to discover, explore, compare, and interpret. It brings together 24 NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations, covering 19 flight investigations and 5 ground or computational fluid dynamics studies.

Data collection and processing

I developed a step by step data collection process using NASA’s PSI repository and its API. First, I queried the repository to identify all 24 investigations under Combustion Science. I then retrieved each investigation’s detailed metadata, including research descriptions, DOIs, publications, file inventories, and experimental table references. Next, I developed and tested the download commands and endpoints to retrieve the experimental CSV files. All 22 available experimental tables were successfully downloaded, and their file sizes were verified against the sizes reported by NASA. I examined the table structures and headers to identify relevant variables, including oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, fuel, and material properties. I also identified inconsistencies in units, missing values, and ambiguous column names to avoid making unsupported assumptions about the data.

Dashboard and functionality

Flamewise transforms this research into an interactive visual exploration experience. Its intelligent ranking system evaluates investigations across six dimensions: material flammability, high oxygen atmospheres, smoke and dust detection, suppression mechanics, partial gravity equivalency, and predictive CFD modeling. Users can explore preset mission scenarios for Lunar Habitats, Mars Habitats, and Spacecraft, or adjust the relevance weights to reflect different research priorities.

The dashboard includes interactive bubble charts, ranked investigation records, an investigation comparison tool, and an oxygen coverage map. Users can filter flight and ground investigations, explore available experimental data, compare up to four studies, and identify areas where data is available or missing. The mission scenarios provide a way to prioritize research for future exploration. They do not imply that the ingested dataset contains actual lunar or Martian partial gravity experiments.

The project also includes AI assisted features: a natural language graph generator that creates custom visualizations and a chat assistant that answers questions using the loaded investigation data. These features use the Google Gemini API and require an API key.

Technology and impact

I developed the dashboard using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, and Chart.js, with Google Gemini for AI functionality. The central design idea came from my preference for visual analysis over reading lengthy technical documents. Different research questions call for different visual representations, so I designed the interface to make complex experimental information easier to navigate through charts, comparisons, filters, and interactive exploration.

Flamewise aims to reduce the effort required to locate relevant NASA combustion research, understand experimental conditions, compare investigations, and identify potential research gaps. It turns a collection of scientific records and experimental tables into a more accessible starting point for research and future space safety investigations.

AI features and demo availability

The project also includes two AI assisted features: a natural language graph generator that creates custom visualizations and a chat assistant that answers questions using the loaded investigation data. Both use the Google Gemini API. These features are implemented but are currently unavailable in the public GitHub deployment because the API key is associated with a personal account and cannot be securely exposed through the static hosting environment. I can demonstrate these capabilities separately during the live presentation using my personal API access, without publishing the key in the repository.
